subject: Life Skills
title: Body Language Clusters
description: A short lesson to help you apply Body Language Clusters.

hook.text: A crossed-arms myth: it does not always mean defensiveness. Sometimes the room is just cold.

buildup.text: Single gestures are unreliable. Body language experts read clusters — three or more signals pointing the same way.

discovery.text: Crossed arms plus leaning back plus avoiding eye contact together suggest discomfort. One alone tells you nothing.

twist.text: Baseline matters. If someone always crosses their arms, it is habit, not a signal. Compare to their normal behavior.

climax.text: Look for sudden changes. A shift from open to closed posture mid-conversation is more telling than any static pose.

punchline.text: Read clusters, not single gestures. Context is everything.

quiz.question: Why are single body language gestures unreliable?
options: A single gesture can have many innocent explanations
Body language varies too much between cultures
